Gifts for student pilots, from first lesson to first solo

The best gift for a student pilot fits the stage they are at. Someone booking a first lesson needs different things from someone preparing for a checkride. Start with one question: what has their instructor actually recommended?

By Pilot Gift Guide · From the team behind ATC · How we choose

IN THIS GUIDEStart with the instructor’s listFor the first few lessonsFor someone already trainingMake a milestone gift personalWhat should you avoid?Our ranked picks

Start with the instructor’s list

Before buying training equipment, find out what the school already supplies and what the instructor expects the student to bring. A duplicate logbook or an incompatible tablet holder is less helpful than a simple gift card. You do not need to understand every piece of equipment: ask the student for a photo or link to their list. If you want to keep the surprise, ask which category is still missing without choosing a model yet.

For the first few lessons

A modest, practical gift is often enough. A logbook can mark the beginning of training if the school has not already supplied one. A pen is easy to add, and a compact light may be useful as the student builds a flight bag. Keep a gift receipt. Avoid buying a complete bundle simply because it says student pilot; the school may have a different syllabus, preferred materials or equipment requirements.

For someone already training

Pay attention to what they carry. A compact flight bag can help if everything currently goes into a general backpack. A kneeboard makes sense only if it fits their exact tablet and they prefer that setup in the cockpit. Ask about the tablet case as well as the iPad model. A headset is a bigger decision: make it a choose-together gift with the student and instructor instead of guessing at connectors or fit.

Make a milestone gift personal

For a first solo or certificate, the story can matter more than the price. A model of the aircraft they actually flew is a better match than a more expensive model of an unrelated airplane. Confirm the type and variant before buying. Add a handwritten note with the date and the moment you are celebrating. For a flight lesson contribution, arrange payment directly with the school and confirm how credit is applied and whether it expires.

What should you avoid?

Do not assume that a flight simulator accessory, training course or navigation subscription matches their instructor’s plan. Ask first. A gift should support training without creating a second system the student has to learn. If you cannot verify compatibility, choose a keepsake or a retailer gift card and let them select their own equipment.

Our ranked picks

Ordered for the audience and purpose of this guide, based on published product information and editorial judgment. Check the source for current specifications and pricing.

  1. 1
    For a first lesson

    ASA pilot logbook

    Listed price: $9.49 · checked Oct 20, 2026

    Why it makes the list: An affordable way to mark the start of flight training. Pair it with a note about the journey ahead, rather than filling in any flight-record pages yourself.

    What to know: Check with their instructor first: they may already have a logbook or use a different format.

    Source: pilotmall.com ↗
  2. 2
    Under $25

    SKILCRAFT B3 Aviator pen

    Listed price: $24.50 · checked Oct 20, 2026

    Why it makes the list: Black ink, red ink and a pencil in one everyday tool. An uncomplicated addition to a practical gift bundle, especially with a handwritten note.

    What to know: Check whether they prefer paper notes; an all-digital pilot may get less use from it.

    Source: pilotmall.com ↗
  3. 3
    A useful little extra

    Flight Gear Aviator’s Light

    Listed price: $29.95 · checked Oct 20, 2026

    Why it makes the list: A compact light with separate red and white controls. It makes sense for the person who likes keeping small, useful tools in their flight bag.

    What to know: Ask what light they already carry; this is an accessory, not a replacement for required equipment.

    Source: sportys.com ↗
  4. 4
    For their next flight

    Flight Gear Stealth Bag

    Listed price: $79.95 · checked Oct 20, 2026

    Why it makes the list: A flight bag is a gift they can use beyond the holidays. This compact backpack-style option is worth a look when their current setup is an overflowing ordinary bag.

    What to know: Compare the listed dimensions with their headset, tablet and usual load before choosing.

    Source: sportys.com ↗
  5. 5
    For the organized pilot

    Flight Gear rotating kneeboard

    Listed price: $22.95 · checked Oct 20, 2026

    Why it makes the list: A practical way to keep a compatible iPad in reach. It is most useful when you already know the pilot wants a kneeboard rather than a mounted tablet.

    What to know: Confirm the exact iPad model, case and preferred cockpit setup with the retailer.

    Source: sportys.com ↗
  6. 6
    A milestone keepsake

    Cessna 172 Skyhawk model

    Listed price: $249.00 · checked Oct 20, 2026

    Why it makes the list: The best model is often the aircraft with a story behind it. This mahogany Skyhawk is especially thoughtful for someone who learned to fly a Cessna 172.

    What to know: Confirm their aircraft type. A 172 and a 182 are different airplanes, even if they look similar.

    Source: pilotmall.com ↗
